page.layout: One printed page (right side of the scan): one main text column on the left, with a narrow marginal note column on the right. Running head at the top, page number at top right. Catchword "us" at the foot of the text column. A faint signature mark at the bottom left. Left-hand page edge is not transcribed.

main_text.p: vota sunt.] Et Paulo ante, [sic itaque nos ad deum expansos ungulæ fodiant, Cruces suspendant, ignes lambant, gladij guttura detruncent, bestiæ insiliant, paratus est ad omne supplicium habitus Orantij Christiani; hoc agite boni Præsides, extorquete animam deo supplicantem pro Imperatore.] Concludo tandem hoc caput, cum illa aurea Apolog. 30. Tertulliani Sententia, Contra quam Marianistæ ne hiscere quidè audeant. [Christianus nullius est hostis, nedum Imperatoris, quem sciens à Deo constitui, necesse est, ut & ipsum diligat, & reverea-tur, & honoret, & salvum velit, cum toto imperio Romano. Colimus ergo Imperatorem, sic quomodo & nobis licet, & ipsi expedit, ut hominem à Deo secundum, & quicquid est, à Deo consecutum, & solo Deo minorem. Hoc & ipsi volet, sic enim omnibus maior est, dum solo Deo minor est. Inde est imperator, unde est & homo potestas unde spiritus.] Et licet hæc aliaque huiusmodi, à Tertulliano, non propter conscientiam, sed in gratiam Gentilium dicta, quod eos scilicet offendere noluerit, in suis Annotationibus in ipsi-us

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Italic passages marked as they appear; "Tertulliani", "Marianistæ" and "Christianus" are set in italic, which is uncertain for "Marianistæ" and "Christianus". The superscript "m" after "aurea" is read as the reference mark for the marginal note "Apolog. 30." The bottom-left mark is read as a signature with a question mark. The left page edge is not transcribed.
